name: Indian-Inspired Beef Kheema with Peas & Basmati Rice

cookwares.name: stainless steel or cast iron skillet

instructions.primary_message: Rinse the rice in a colander and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt; bring to a boil.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ cups basmati rice
3 cups water
⅜ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tomatoes
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
1 ½ small bunches cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Small dice the tomatoes; transfer to a medium bowl.
Once the water is boiling, reduce the heat to low, stir, and cover. Cook until the liquid is absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Remove from the heat and let the rice stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion; transfer to a small bowl.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onions to the skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
While the onion cooks, peel and mince the ginger; transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to the bowl of ginger.
Add curry powder to the bowl of ginger and garlic.
Add the spice mixture to the onions; cook, stirring constantly, for about 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking apart into smaller pieces, until browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the tomato, water and season with salt; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ cup water
1 ½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and chop the leaves.
Add the peas and half of the cilantro (save the rest for garnishing) to the skillet; stir to combine and cook until the peas are warmed through, 2 to 3 minutes.
Divide the rice between plates, top with the beef kheema, and garnish with the remaining cilantro. Enjoy!
